summary: Real RETURNDATA behavior fix, but no co-evolving behavioral contract for the changed executable routine. The same-hunk contract token belongs to a newly added logical predicate, not CreateReturn.

Shanghai fork configuration and Java dispatch/tests are added, while the only Dafny contract-token change is the new verify-false proof lemma. No existing executable routine and its behavioral contract co-evolve.
Cancun support changes executable/configuration semantics and tests, but the contract hit is a newly added verify-false proof lemma, not a changed contract on the executable behavior.

Commit intentionally removes specifications to speed verification. Bytecode function bodies are not semantically changed; remaining changes in memory/bytes are specification commenting or brace/indent formatting. Thus there is contract change without executable-behavior change.

There is no historical old FNeed implementation or old FNeed contract to cross. The patch introduces a new API declaration atomically; splitting its new requires from its new body would fabricate an old/new pair rather than recover one.

Like U043, this is an addition from a parent with no FNeed declaration. There is no historical old body/old contract endpoint. Comments make the patch bytes distinct, so the frozen exact-byte dedupe correctly retains a separate unit even though the semantic addition is closely related.
Three predicates are newly introduced with their requires clauses and bodies; there is no historical old declaration/body/contract counterpart to pair.

AddEdge's returned automaton expression is unchanged; an assertion is replaced by a ghost lemma call and the new lemma carries the requires/ensures hit. Proof scaffolding changes, executable result semantics do not co-evolve with a behavioral contract.

CLI/printing behavior changes; mechanical requires hits occur inside Filter/ToDot lambdas as local proof obligations. No changed behavioral contract of the changed driver behavior forms an old/new pair.

BuildSeg switches from explicit redundant delta helper arguments to constructors that compute/use the new representation; its existing requires is unchanged. Contract-token deletions are from removed proof lemmas/helpers, not a co-evolving BuildSeg behavioral contract.
Only a proof lemma with ensures is added (plus a comment typo fix); there is no executable implementation transition.
AddKeyVal, proof lemmas, and IsReverseMap are new declarations. Even though AddKeyVal has both a body and contract, no historical old AddKeyVal exists; a four-way old/new pair would be invented.

Existing DFS code is refactored for proof discharge and a new PathHelperLemma is added. DFS requires/ensures/decreases are unchanged; all added contract clauses belong to the new lemma, not to the changed DFS behavior.
Only comments plus a new proof lemma WeakestPreMonotonic are added. The existing FastWeakestPreOperands implementation and its requires/ensures remain semantically unchanged.
SeqToSet is a wholly new declaration whose body and two ensures clauses appear together. The parent has no old SeqToSet body/contract, so no historical cross-pair exists without invention.

A new weakest-precondition fixpoint subsystem (Fix, UpdateValues, MaxNatSeq, ComputeWPreOperands, HasNoErrorState) is added with bodies and contracts together. ToHTML is extended to consume the new result, but its preconditions are unchanged. There is no old contract/body counterpart for the added subsystem.

Driver/HTML executable/output behavior changes substantially, but no target routine gains or changes a behavioral requires/ensures contract. Contract-token hits are lambda requires moved/retained at callback sites; assertions are proof obligations, not public behavioral contracts.

Frozen N0 is inconsistent with the exact patch. Five new non-ghost helper declarations (StackEffect, CapEffect, WpOp, IsJump, WpCap) are added, each with requires i < |xs| and a semantic body. The parent contains none of them. This is a new-declaration/non-pairable transition, i.e. N1, not N0. Commit subject `Formatting.` is misleading and must not control classification.
StackToCond and StackToCondHelper are new declarations born with their contracts; the only pre-existing change is an opacity attribute on And, not an old/new behavioral-contract pair.
StackToHTML and StackToHTMLHelper are wholly new declarations; parent CFGState has neither, so no historical old body/contract exists.

Proof-object/CFG-code generator behavior changes substantially, but ToDafny and PrintProofObjectBody retain their own requires/decreases contracts; many apparent requires/ensures are strings emitted into generated Dafny, while newly contracted CFGCheckerToDafny/PrintCFGVerifierBody declarations have no old counterparts.

Existing PrintProofObjectBody changes the Dafny text it emits while its own requires/decreases remain unchanged; CFGRefineToDafny is a new method with new preconditions. Generated requires/ensures string edits are output data, not a co-evolving contract on the generator itself.

SplitTrueAndFalse strengthens one postcondition, but its returned partition computation is unchanged; added lemmas/asserts/attributes are verification machinery. This is contract/proof evolution without a semantic executable-body transition of the same pair.
Core-library edits are whitespace/comment formatting; test code adds expect diagnostics but PrintPath's precondition is unchanged. No executable routine and its behavioral contract co-evolve.
Existing PathHelperLemma contract is unchanged; the patch fills only the lemma proof body with quantified proof blocks/assertions. No executable routine behavior and its boundary contract co-evolve.

The exact patch adds new executable declarations Peek, Push1, Push2, Push20, Dup1-Dup4, Swap1, and Swap2 with bodies/contracts while existing opcode bodies remain unchanged and their postconditions are strengthened. Frozen N0/impl_kind=none misses these born-together declarations; the correct primary negative class is N1 because they have no historical old counterpart.

UpdateValues replaces a MapP expression with a sequence comprehension to avoid a Java-backend issue and adds an assertion, but the outer UpdateValues requires/ensures are unchanged. This is an implementation/tooling substitution without co-evolving behavioral contract.

Dup5 and Swap3 are introduced as new declarations with contracts and bodies; PrettyInstruction is updated to call the newly born Swap3. The parent has no Dup5 or Swap3 declaration, so no historical old body/contract pair exists.

The frozen N1 label misses a real existing-declaration repair: parent Swap3 swaps indices 0 and 2 and specifies index-2 effects despite requires >3; head Swap3 swaps 0 and 3 and changes the corresponding contract, including ensures s' == Swap(s,3). Thus executable body and behavioral contract co-evolve. However the same patch also adds many concrete Push/Dup/Swap/Log declarations, strengthens many existing opcode contracts, and rewrites pretty-printer mappings, so there is no unique whole-patch two-factor split preserving exact endpoints. Corrected class: E1, not E0.

SplitTrueAndFalse drops two redundant/strong proof postconditions and rewrites proof scaffolding: ghost lemma calls become cached recursive result plus assertions. The extensional result remains [xsTrue] or [xsTrue] + SplitTrueAndFalse(xsFalse,...); no semantic executable result transition accompanies the contract change.

Only the body of the existing proof lemma decode_encode_uint64_seq_id is strengthened with assertions and lemma calls; the live lemma contract is unchanged. The additional alternative lemma is commented out. No executable behavioral-contract co-evolution occurs.
